TGFβ induces early activation of the RhoA small GTPase in Smad2/ 3-independent manner via the Src kinase and its effector the Vav2 guanine nucleotide-exchange factor.
the early activation of the small GTPase RHOA by TGFbeta is Smad2-independent and involves Src and the guanine nucleotides exchange factor Vav2.
TGFβ-induced activation of small GTPases RhoA and B is Smad2-independent and involves the tyrosine kinase c-Src and the guanine nucleo-tide exchange factor Vav2.

the identification of novel mechanisms that regulate the early Rho activation by a growth factor, TGFβ, which may be of importance for understanding the mechanisms of cell motility and migration.
the identification of new mechanisms involved in the early TGF β-induced Rho activation and the regulation of cell motility.
the early signaling events that regulate the RhoA activation in response to TGFβ.

the early Rho activation by the TGFβ is a Src-dependent and Smad3-independent process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TGFβ-induced rapid activation of Rho GEFs and RhoA is a novel Smad-independent signaling pathway that involves the non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase, Src.

TGFβ can induce rapid Rho activation through Src/Vav2-GEFs in Smad2/Smad3-deficient cells, and that this activation does not involve Smad2/ Smad3 signaling.
